_comment: Curated compare moments for the LOCAL-ONLY speller comparison (viz/src/compare.ts). step is 1-based, as in the URL. mode is ours. Copied to compare/moments.json by viz/build.mjs only outside CI.

moments.title: Purcell, Cold Song m. 27: one chord, two spellings
moments.text: A B♭-minor triad struck twice, half a beat apart: PKSpell writes D♭ on beat 2, then C♯ on beat 2.5 (B♭–C♯–F). Ours keeps D♭ both times.

moments.title: Shostakovich, Quartet No. 8 m. 92: a unison split
moments.text: Two voices on the same E: PKSpell spells one E and the other F♭. Co-sounding notes of one pitch share one spelling.

moments.title: Chopin, Prelude No. 20 m. 8: our own split (two-pass)
moments.text: Our mistake: two-pass spells a struck D♭-major chord C♯–F–A♭, breaking the triad. ps13, Temperley, Chew & Chen, PKSpell and our own Core, real-time and look-ahead modes all write D♭.

moments.title: Chopin, Prelude No. 4 m. 6: B major with E♭
moments.text: B, D♯ and F♯ struck together: ps13 writes E♭ (B–E♭–F♯, a diminished fourth inside a major triad). Temperley, Chew & Chen and music21 do the same; ours writes D♯.

moments.title: Grieg, Morning Mood m. 9: G♯ major with C
moments.text: A struck G♯-major chord: Chew & Chen write C for the third (G♯–C–D♯), and so does ps13. Ours writes B♯, as Grieg did.

moments.title: Schumann, Träumerei m. 7: A major with D♭
moments.text: A struck A7 chord (A–C♯–E–G): Temperley spells the bass C♯ as D♭, a diminished fourth above A. Ours writes C♯.

moments.title: Beethoven, Moonlight m. 26: G♯ major with C and E♭
moments.text: music21's default MIDI spelling has one fixed name per key, so the G♯-major chord comes out G♯–C–E♭. Ours writes G♯–B♯–D♯, as Beethoven did.

moments.title: Mozart, K. 545 m. 68: they are right, we are wrong
moments.text: A diminished-seventh sonority F♯–C–E♭: Mozart writes E♭, and so do Temperley, ps13 and Chew & Chen. Ours writes D♯. Dim7 chords are our hardest case.

moments.title: Chopin, Prelude No. 4 m. 16: they are right, we are wrong
moments.text: Chopin's line is C♯–B–A♯ over E–G. Two-pass flips the line to D♭–C♭–B♭ over E–G; ps13 keeps Chopin's sharps.
